findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses three independent fields (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool) that allow inconsistent state combinations. For example, is_sent=true with status="pending" is silently representable, and there is no enforced ordering (e.g., cannot send without validating first).
findings.failure_mode: Programmer can construct or mutate a LedgerWorkflow into an invalid state without compiler enforcement, leading to undefined workflow semantics and silent data corruption at runtime.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single enum typestate (e.g., enum LedgerState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }). Remove the bool/String fields entirely so only valid states are constructable.

findings.problem: id: String and status: String are primitive types with no domain invariants encoded in their types. Any string value is accepted for id, and status has no compile-time guarantees.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs or unrecognized status values propagate through the system undetected. No domain validation at the type boundary.
findings.fix: Introduce newtype wrappers: pub struct LedgerId(String) with a fallible constructor that validates format, and replace the status field entirely with a domain enum typestate as noted above.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LedgerWorkflow directly instead of Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>. There is no precondition check (e.g., item must be validated before being sent) and no typed error for invalid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Calling mark_sent on an unvalidated ledger silently transitions it to sent, violating domain workflow invariants. No caller can handle the failure case with a typed error.
findings.fix: Change the signature to pub fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>. Validate the pre-state in the typestate enum and return a domain error (e.g., LedgerError::NotValidated) if the transition is invalid.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs a side-effect-bearing mutation (setting is_sent=true, updating status) inside what should be a pure calculation layer. The function has no separation between domain validation (pure) and the action of recording the transition.
findings.failure_mode: Business logic is entangled with mutation, making it impossible to unit-test the state transition rules in isolation from the workflow struct mutation.
findings.fix: Separate into pure validation: pub fn can_send(&LedgerWorkflow) -> bool (or better, use pattern matching on the typestate enum), and a shell action that applies the transition with explicit error handling.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing external code to mutate id, status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms directly without any domain logic or validation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set item.is_sent = true without going through mark_sent, completely bypassing the (already-absent) validation logic. Fields are mutable from outside the module.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide only domain-approved constructors and transition methods. With the typestate enum approach, construction itself enforces validity.

residual_risk: The typestate model is entirely absent — illegal states (sent-but-not-validated, inconsistent status/flag pairs) are fully representable and constructable. This is a fundamental DDD contract violation that prevents any meaningful correctness guarantees. Proof obligations cannot be derived until the type model is repaired.
